changes.before: Replace the proc with ->(value) { value } and still call it with no arguments. What happens?
changes.after: A lambda is a callable that checks how many inputs it receives. An ordinary proc can handle missing inputs differently.

before: proc { |value| value } makes a Proc. ->(value) { value } makes a lambda, which is also a Proc object with different calling rules.

A lambda requires its declared argument count unless defaults or rest parameters allow otherwise. This one-parameter lambda raises ArgumentError when called with no arguments.

This lambda accepts one value and returns it unchanged. The first call supplies 3; the second deliberately supplies no argument and stops with an arity error. It is an error demonstration, not a complete successful program.
```ruby
reader = ->(value) { value }
puts reader.call(3)
reader.call
```
This stops with ArgumentError.
The simple ordinary proc below accepts no arguments and binds value to nil. return inside an ordinary proc also differs from return inside a lambda; do not treat them as interchangeable.
nil.inspect returns the text nil, unlike puts nil which writes an empty line.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
reader = proc { |value| value }
puts reader.call.inspect
```
Expected output or behavior: nil. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare the same argument list with a lambda and an ordinary proc; do not use nonlocal return outside a valid defining method. You may trace it without a Ruby interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

This proc has one input named value.
The call supplies no input. Inspect makes its missing result visible as text.
In this ordinary proc the missing input gets nil.

before.question: Replace the proc with ->(value) { value } and still call it with no arguments. What happens?
choices: It prints nil because lambdas always pad missing arguments.
It prints zero because missing numeric arguments default to zero.
It raises ArgumentError because this lambda requires one argument.
before.explanation: The lambda enforces its one-parameter arity; the original ordinary proc tolerated the missing argument.

after.question: Replace the proc with a lambda that requires one input. What happens when it gets no inputs?
after.explanation: The lambda requires one input and received none.
